name: Allium

project_scope.canonical_install: source-pool pair curated through 2026-10-10 installer; scientific range unresolved

look_here_first: Inspect an intact papery spathe and its veins, then count flowers versus aerial bulbils; flower color and absence of bulbils alone are unreliable.
shared_traits: Bulbous herbs with onion odor, basal linear leaves, a leafless scape and umbel.
Six tepals, six stamens and superior ovary; capsules develop from flowers.

comparison.drummondii: Usually 2–3 bracts, about one-veined (FNA). Local descriptions may differ; prioritize intact material.

comparison.canadense: Loose 0–60-flowered umbel; aerial bulbils may replace flowers in some varieties.

comparison.drummondii: About 10–30 cm × 1–3(–5) mm; overlap requires multiple traits.

cautions: A. canadense includes several varieties; bulbil absence does not exclude it.
Onion odor distinguishes many Allium from Nothoscordum, but does not separate these two onions.
Use flower and fruit structure, not tepal color.

lookalikes.name: Zephyranthes
lookalikes.difference: Inferior ovary, often solitary larger flower

photo_targets: Whole umbel with flowers and bulbils
Flower face and side with scale

handoffs.need: Dependency resolved: both species already in canonical manifest. No additional installation needed.
Matched reproductive macro views for both species.

status: two canonical species compared; same-scale spathe-vein diagnostic photos pending; native-range statuses preserved

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: Unopened or intact papery umbel spathe
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Count bracts and veins on each bract. Three to four multiveined bracts favor A. canadense; two to three approximately one-veined bracts favor A. drummondii.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: Whole umbel with all flowers and aerial bulbils visible
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Bulbils can support A. canadense but absence is not exclusion; predominantly flowered umbels occur in both.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: Several basal leaves and mature flowers with millimeter scale
look_here_first_sequence.decision: A. canadense generally has longer/broader leaves; A. drummondii usually has narrower leaves and 5–20 mm flower pedicels. Leaf sizes overlap.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: Six tepals, six stamens, superior ovary and bulb odor
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Confirm Allium against Nothoscordum and rain lilies; do not use tepal color to separate the two Allium species.

species_comparison_matrix.drummondii: Usually 2–3 bracts, about one vein each

species_comparison_matrix.canadense: Loose, 0–60 flowers; bulbils variable by variety
Measure intact flowers; no non-overlapping value verified in current species card
species_comparison_matrix.drummondii: Pedicels 5–20 mm in current canonical card
